## Summary

I implemented the unified container replication service by removing the zero-copy boolean flag, touching only source files (no `test/` files, per the constraint — the verification system applies test patches).

**`GrpcReplicationService.java`**
- Constructor now takes only `ContainerReplicationSource source, ContainerImporter importer`.
- Removed the `zeroCopyEnabled` field and the conditional; the zero-copy marshallers are now always constructed (default was `true`).
- `bindServiceWithZeroCopy()` no longer short-circuits on a disabled flag — it always binds the zero-copy method descriptors.

**`ReplicationServer.java`**
- `init(boolean enableZeroCopy)` → `init()`; the `GrpcReplicationService` is now built with the two-arg constructor.
- Removed the `ZEROCOPY_ENABLE_KEY`/`ZEROCOPY_ENABLE_DEFAULT` constants, the `@Config zeroCopyEnable` field, and its `isZeroCopyEnable()`/`setZeroCopyEnable()` accessors.

I left the unrelated EC-client gRPC zero-copy path (`XceiverServerGrpc`/`GrpcXceiverService`, `ozone.ec.grpc.zerocopy.enabled`) untouched, since it's a separate mechanism outside the container replication service's scope.

The test-suite refactoring you described (deleting `TestGrpcReplicationServiceWithZeroCopy`, `AbstractTestECKeyOutputStream`, `TestECKeyOutputStreamWithZeroCopy`, and making `TestECKeyOutputStream` standalone) lives under `src/test/java/` and will be applied by the verification system's test patches — the source changes above make those refactors compile.
